title.en: Spatial graph with explicit relationship meaning

summary: Use depth to organize a network while keeping edge direction, grouping and algorithm state readable.
objective: Use depth to organize a network while keeping edge direction, grouping and algorithm state readable.
example_prompts: Use spatial graph with explicit relationship meaning for the scene, preserving its model and user controls.

principles: Give spatial grouping a declared purpose; do not imply that geometric distance is measured latency or similarity unless it is.
A simpler layered view may communicate a dense graph better than an arbitrary cloud.
implementation: Separate node identity, graph connectivity and chosen layout positions.
Encode edge direction consistently and make crossings selectable or inspectable.
Highlight algorithm state through a separate channel from structural groups, with an optional flat view.
observable_checks: Changing layout preserves node IDs, edge endpoints and algorithm results.
An inspected edge states its direction and relationship meaning.

creative_affordances: Adapt the layout, visual treatment and timing to the task; these are reusable design proposals, not mandatory templates.
known_limits: Authored interaction/presentation guidance; no new scientific claim, accessibility certification or runtime verification is asserted.
